text:
Beside me without cease the Demon stirs;

Around me he floats like an impalpable air;

I swallow him and feel how he burns my lungs,

Filling them with guilty and infinite desire.


Sometimes, for he knows of my love for Art,

He takes on the appearance of the most seductive woman,

And, resorting to specious flatterer's pretexts,

Accustoms my lips to depraved filters.


Thus he carries me far from the gaze of God,

Panting and undone by fatigue, to the center

Of the deep and lonely plains of Boredom,


And casts before my eyes, filled with confusion,

Stained garments and half-open wounds,

And the bloody apparatus that lives in Destruction!

translation.title: Destruction
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the demon as temptation, artistic seduction, boredom, and visible machinery of destruction.
